Name: Matteo Ricci
Summary: Italian Jesuit missionary (1552-1610) who spent nearly thirty years in China, learning its language and culture and winning a hearing at the imperial court.
Contribution: He presented Christianity in Chinese terms, translated works of science and philosophy in both directions, and opened a respectful path for the gospel in China that later missionaries followed. His approach of cultural accommodation became a model, and a controversy, for missions.
KeyWorks: The True Meaning of the Lord of Heaven
Testimony: He lived in China until his death in Beijing, dressed as a scholar, and was buried there by imperial favour.
